title: Preparation and Characterization of Novel HDL-mimicking Nanoparticles for Nerve Growth Factor Encapsulation
protocol: Dissolve phosphatidylcholine, sphingomyelin, phosphatidylserine, cholesteryl oleate, and D-α-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol succinate in ethanol to prepare stock solutions at 1 mg/mL each.
Mix 10 µL of NGF (1 mg/mL in water) with 10 µL of protamine USP (1 mg/mL in water).
Let the NGF and protamine complex stand for 10 min at room temperature.
Add 59 µL of PC, 11 µL of SM, 4 µL of PS, 15 µL of CO, and 45 µL of TPGS to a glass vial.
Mix the excipients under a gentle nitrogen stream for about 5 min until an oily thin film forms at the bottom of the glass vial.
Add 1 mL of ultrapure water to the vial containing the thin film.
Homogenize at 9,500 rpm (8,600 x g) for 5 min at room temperature to form the prototype NPs.
Add the complex prepared in step 1.2 to the prototype NPs.
Incubate at 37 °C for 30 min with stirring using a small stirring bar in the glass vial.
Cool the NPs by stirring at room temperature for another 30 min.
Add 106 µL of Apo A-I (1.49 mg/mL) and stir at room temperature overnight to form the final NGF HDL-mimicking NPs.
Measure the particle size using a particle analyzer as per the manufacturer's instructions.
Measure the zeta potential using a particle analyzer as per the manufacturer's instructions.
Transfer 15 mL of Sepharose 4B-CL suspension to a 50-mL beaker.
Stir the bead suspension using a glass rod and pour some into a column (30 cm length × 1 cm diameter, with a glass frit at the bottom).
Gently tap the column to get rid of bubbles.
Allow the solvent to drain and the beads to settle for a few minutes.
Continue to add the remaining suspension.
Rinse the inside wall of the column to clean the beads.
Drain the solvent until the solvent level is slightly above the top of the stationary phase.
Wash and condition the column with 20 mL of 1x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, containing 137 mM NaCl, 2.7 mM KCl, 8 mM Na2HPO4, and 2 mM KH2PO4).
Load 200 µL of NGF solution onto the gel filtration column.
Elute with 1x PBS and collect a total of 12 fractions (1 mL each).
Measure the concentration of NGF in each fraction using a Sandwich ELISA kit.
Detect NGF from fractions 6 to 10 using the Sandwich ELISA kit.
Obtain a chromatogram of unloaded NGF on the column.
Wash the column with 20 mL of PBS.
Load 200 µL of the NPs onto the column.
Elute with 1x PBS and collect a total of 12 fractions (1 mL each).
Measure the intensity of particles in each fraction using the particle size analyzer.
Detect the NGF NPs from fractions 2 to 4.
Load 200 µL of NGF HDL-mimicking NPs onto the column.
Elute with 1x PBS and collect a total of 12 fractions (1 mL each).
Measure the unloaded NGF concentration from fractions 6 to 10 using the Sandwich ELISA kit.
Mix NGF fractions 6 to 10 together to calculate unloaded NGF.
Calculate the entrapment efficiency of NGF using the equation: %EE = (1 - unloaded NGF/total NGF added into NP) x 100%.
Prepare free NGF at a concentration of 10 µg/mL in water for testing.
Prepare NGF HDL-mimicking nanoparticles at a concentration of 10 µg/mL for testing.
Pre-treat dialysis tubes according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Prepare 5% bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS as release medium.
Warm up 30 mL of release medium in a 50-mL centrifuge tube to 37 °C with 135 rpm shaking speed.
Add 400 µL of release medium into each dialysis tube.
Quickly add 200 µL of the tested sample to each dialysis tube for sufficient volume for dialysis.
Close the dialysis tubes and quickly immerse them in the release medium.
Withdraw 100 µL of release medium from outside each dialysis tube as the time 0 sample.
Immediately place the withdrawn samples into -20 °C for later analysis.
Add 100 µL of fresh release medium to replace the withdrawn sample at each time point.
At 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 24, 48, and 72 h, withdraw 100 µL of release medium from each dialysis tube.
Replace the withdrawn samples with 100 µL of fresh medium at each time point.
Immediately place the withdrawn samples into -20 °C for later analysis.
After 72 h, take out all samples from -20 °C and thaw them at room temperature.
Measure the NGF concentrations of the release samples using the Sandwich ELISA kit.
Culture PC12 cells in RPMI-1640 medium supplemented with 10% heat-inactivated horse serum, 5% fetal bovine serum, 100 µg/mL streptomycin, and 100 units/mL penicillin.
Maintain the cells in a humidified incubator at 37 °C and with 5% CO2.
When the cells reach ~70-80% confluence, remove the culture medium and wash the cells with 1x PBS (approximately 2 mL per 10 cm2 culture surface area).
Remove the wash solution.
Trypsinize the cells by adding 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA solution (0.25% trypsin and 1 mM EDTA; 0.5 mL per 10 cm2 culture surface area) to the flask and incubate at 37 °C until most cells are detached.
Add two volumes of culture medium and spin down at 180 x g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 5 mL of culture medium.
Filter the cells through a 22 G, ½ inch needle to break cell clusters.
Split the cells at a ratio of 1:3 into a new cell culture flask.
After incubating overnight, remove unattached PC12 cells.
Allow the attached cells to remain for further growth.
Repeat this procedure for 3 passages to select the subculture of PC12 that has a strong adhesion property.
Pre-coat a 6-well plate with 800 µL/well of rat tail collagen type I (100 µg/mL).
Trypsinize the selected PC12 cells as described in step 4.2 and filter them through a 22 G, ½ inch needle to break the cell clusters.
Count the cells with a hemocytometer.
Seed the cells overnight at a density of 10,000 cells/well in the pre-coated 6-well plate in step 4.5 to allow the cells to attach to the plate.
Dilute free NGF (10 µg/mL) and NGF HDL-mimicking NPs (10 µg/mL) with the culture medium to prepare 0.5, 1, 5, 10, 50, and 100 ng/mL concentrations.
Remove 2 mL of medium from each well and replace with 2 mL of the diluted free NGF or NGF HDL-mimicking NPs.
Culture for 4 days.
On day 4, change the medium to fresh medium containing the corresponding treatment and continue the treatment for another 3 days.
On day 7, visualize the cells with an inverted light microscope.
Image each well at random spots under 10X magnification.
Use adult BALB/c mice (male, 25-30 g) to test the tissue distribution of NGF NPs.
Randomly divide the mice into three groups of 3 mice per group.
Restrain a mouse using a cone-shaped plastic restraint and wipe the tail with ethanol to promote vasodilation and the visibility of the vein.
Inject 100 µL of either saline, free NGF, or NGF HDL-mimicking NPs through the tail veins at a dose of 40 µg/kg of NGF.
Anesthetize mice using 3% inhaled isoflurane in oxygen at a flow rate of 2 L/min.
Perform a tail and toe pinch to determine the depth of anesthesia.
Collect blood by cardiac puncture, withdrawing approximately 1 mL of blood from the heart.
Euthanize each mouse by cervical dislocation.
Place the mouse carcass in dorsal recumbency.
Open the abdomen using surgical scissors.
Move fat and intestine aside with a cotton swab to expose liver, spleen, and kidney.
Harvest these tissues and rinse them in 1x PBS to clean blood.
Immediately centrifuge blood samples at 3,400 x g and 4 °C for 5 min to obtain plasma.
Store the plasma and tissues at -80 °C until analysis.
Move tissue samples from -80 °C to 4 °C.
Suspend 100 mg of tissue sample in a 10x volume of extraction buffer.
Homogenize the suspension at 10,000 rpm and 4 °C for 5 min.
Sacrifice two untreated mice to collect blank plasma and tissues as described above.
Prepare NGF standard solutions using blank plasma or blank tissue homogenates.
Determine concentrations of NGF in plasma and tissue homogenates using the Sandwich ELISA kit.
